themes_detail.label: Garbage collection collapse
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints spiked to 6 this week versus a 1.9 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (up 220%), signaling a potential sanitation service breakdown in Morningside Heights just as the district has been repeatedly requesting additional sanitation trucks from the city.
evidence: 6 residential disposal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average (220% spike, z-score: 5.28)
Missed collection complaints also spiked 2 weeks ago: 6 complaints vs. 0.4 weekly average (1500% spike, z-score: 8.08)
Community board has repeatedly requested new sanitation trucks in annual budgets—unresolved multi-year ask
reporting_angles: Interview residents about missed pickups this week; check if collection route was changed or trucks reassigned
Analyze whether Sanitation Department is understaffed or under-equipped in CD 109 relative to other Manhattan districts

themes_detail.label: Dead animals and pest emergency
themes_detail.summary: Three dead animal complaints and unsanitary animal complaints on private property spiked 1100% and 900% respectively in the last 2 weeks (3 dead animals vs. 0.2 weekly average; 5 unsanitary animal cases vs. 0.5 average), alongside emergency response team complaints also up 1100%, suggesting a potential public health or pest control crisis.
evidence: Dead animal complaints: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
Unsanitary animal complaints on private property: 5 complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average (900% spike, z-score: 6.36)
Emergency Response Team complaints: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
Community board has been requesting rat and mosquito control funding for multiple years—chronic unmet need
reporting_angles: Map the geography of dead animal/pest complaints to identify cluster; interview Health Department about outbreak response
Investigate whether sanitation backlog (missed collections) is attracting rodents and attracting predators

themes_detail.label: Building exterior deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about building exteriors (OUTSIDE BUILDING) and special building inspections spiked 567% and 540% respectively last week (5 complaints vs. 0.8 baseline; 4 complaints vs. 0.6 baseline), suggesting potential widespread structural or code violations affecting the housing stock.
evidence: OUTSIDE BUILDING complaints: 5 complaints last week vs. 0.8 weekly average (567% spike, z-score: 6.43)
Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints: 4 complaints last week vs. 0.6 weekly average (540% spike, z-score: 6.97)
376 DOB filings in past 90 days (332 alterations) suggest active construction; spike may indicate inspection enforcement or visible code issues
reporting_angles: Cross-reference SPIT complaints with DOB permit data to see if inspectors flagged violations at specific addresses
Interview Department of Buildings about whether exterior complaint surge indicates a pattern of deferred maintenance or failed recent inspections

themes_detail.label: Parking enforcement surge
themes_detail.summary: Blocked driveway complaints jumped to 10 two weeks ago versus a 4.5 weekly average (122% spike, z-score: 4.92), pointing to a recent enforcement action or parking crackdown in the district.
evidence: Blocked driveway complaints: 10 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 4.5 weekly average (122% spike, z-score: 4.92)
Illegal parking remains high overall (1177 complaints over 90 days), but spike suggests a specific recent event or policy change
reporting_angles: Determine if NYPD or Department of Transportation initiated new enforcement action 2-3 weeks ago
Check if a specific block or intersection is affected or if it's district-wide

themes_detail.label: Long-term housing development tension
themes_detail.summary: Hill Top Apartments (1727 Amsterdam Avenue) remains in public review under ULURP, reflecting ongoing neighborhood concerns about land use and zoning that the community board has flagged annually as a priority for Department of City Planning intervention.
evidence: Hill Top Apartments ULURP application in public review stage, pending post-hearing follow-up and future votes
Community board has requested study of land use and zoning to match current/future neighborhood needs—repeated annually, unresolved
376 DOB filings (majority alterations) indicate high development/renovation activity in a district still grappling with land use planning
reporting_angles: Attend upcoming Hill Top Apartments review; interview residents and community board on zoning concerns
Broader investigation: Has Department of City Planning responded to community board's multi-year zoning study request?
